mainTopic: The doubtful מצורע's conditional offerings, and רבי אליעזר's rule that unfit limbs may go up on the מזבח 'as wood'
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי שמעון's plan for a person who may or may not be a מצורע. He brings his לוג of oil with a condition, and if he is not a מצורע the sprinkling counts only 'as wood.' The גמרא handles three problems with this plan. Leftover oil that never had a קמיצה is redeemed. The redemption happens inside the עזרה, because the oil becomes חולין there on its own. רבי שמעון allows donating oil here because it is needed to purify a person. רב רחומי then suggests making the animal an אשם תלוי instead, and tries to prove רבי שמעון's view from this. רבינא rejects him: the מצורע brings a lamb, but an אשם תלוי must be a ram. A new משנה follows about חטאת limbs mixed with עולה limbs. רבי אליעזר puts them all on the מזבח and treats the חטאת meat as wood, learning this from 'לא יעלו לריח ניחח'. The רבנן limit that rule to leaven and honey. A ברייתא of רבי יהודה says the real argument is about blemished limbs. The גמרא then asks why רבי אליעזר does not treat a רובע or נרבע the same way, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The sprinkling is done 'for the sake of wood'
steps.stepSummary: The end of an answer from the previous page: the כהן makes a condition, so if the person is not a מצורע, the sprinkling of oil is not counted as a real עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from the previous page. The כהן sprinkles the oil with a condition, so if this oil is only a נדבה, the sprinkling does not count as a real sacrificial act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a נדבה of oil should not have the special מצורע sprinklings done with it. The answer compares this to bringing something up 'for the sake of wood.' The action happens, but it is not treated as an offering rite. Because of the condition, nothing improper is done to a נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: for the sake of wood, meaning not as a real offering rite
a voluntary gift offering
a person with צרעת who brings offerings to become pure

phrases.english: For the sake of wood.
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer from the previous page: the sprinkling counts like something done 'just as wood,' not as a real offering act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from the previous daf about the oil sprinklings
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conditional stipulation that takes away the sprinkling's status as an עבודה
steps.terutzMaskana: If the person is not a מצורע, the sprinkling of oil is just like an act done 'for wood' and is not a real rite.

steps.title: Some of the oil was never permitted by a קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the plan. The leftover oil has to be dealt with, and some of it is a small amount that never had a קמיצה taken for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the remainder that needs to be dealt with, and there is that little bit for which no handful was taken!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the plan. If the oil turns out to be a נדבה, part of it was never made permitted by a קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדבה of oil becomes permitted by taking a handful (קמיצה) from it. The concern is that after the handful is removed, the לוג is filled up again. That small added amount never had a handful taken for it, so it is left in a status with no way to be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: the remainder of the oil after the handful is taken
he takes a handful (קְמִיצָה)
a small bit

phrases.english: But there is the remainder
which needs filling up (or, in other versions, eating),
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'fill them up' (the round brackets); the corrected wording in square brackets says 'eat them.'

phrases.english: and there is that small bit
for which he did not take a handful!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new problem with the conditional לוג plan
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan of bringing the לוג as a conditional נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the oil is a נדבה, every part of it must be permitted through קמיצה. The added bit never was, so it is left without a solution.

steps.title: He redeems the leftover bit
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the כהן redeems that bit of oil, which takes away its holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the leftover oil gets redeemed (פדיון), so its holiness is removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil cannot be permitted by קמיצה, so it is taken out of holiness another way. Its value is given to the הקדש, and the oil becomes חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: he redeems (פִּדְיוֹן)

phrases.english: That he redeems it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא about the bit with no קמיצה
steps.terutzMaskana: The leftover oil is redeemed and becomes חולין.

steps.title: Where could he redeem it?
steps.stepSummary: Both choices seem to fail. Inside, he brings חולין into the עזרה. Outside, the oil becomes פסול because it left the עזרה (יוצא).
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does he redeem it? If inside, he is bringing non-holy oil into the courtyard. If outside, it becomes disqualified for having gone out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by asking where the redemption could take place, and shows that both options seem to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the עזרה, redeeming the oil would seem to create חולין in the עזרה, which is forbidden. Taking it outside first makes it פסול as יוצא before it is redeemed. This is a trap with two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: inside (the עזרה)
outside
non-holy items in the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
a holy item that left its proper area and became פסול

phrases.english: That he redeems it, where?

phrases.aramaic: אִי גַּוַּואי – קָא מְעַיֵּיל חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה,
phrases.english: If inside, he is bringing non-holy items into the courtyard;
if outside, it becomes disqualified by going out!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he redeems the oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible places for the redemption run into a prohibition, so redemption seems impossible.

steps.title: Inside: the oil becomes חולין by itself
steps.stepSummary: He redeems it inside. This is allowed because he did not bring חולין in; the oil simply became חולין where it already was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is inside; it becomes non-holy on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the redemption is done inside the עזרה, and this does not break the rule against bringing חולין in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule forbids actively bringing חולין into the עזרה. Here the oil entered while it was holy and only turned into חולין there. That is not 'bringing in' חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (it is the first option)
by itself, on its own

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on חולין in the עזרה is about bringing them in. Something that becomes חולין while already inside is not a problem.

phrases.english: Actually, inside;
they become non-holy by themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'where' challenge by choosing the first option
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Redeeming inside counts as bringing חולין into the עזרה
steps.terutzMaskana: Holy items that become חולין inside are not forbidden, because nothing was brought in.

steps.title: But רבי שמעון holds oil cannot be donated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the whole plan from רבי שמעון's own view that a person cannot donate oil as a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון said one may not donate oil!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how this plan can follow רבי שמעון's view, since he himself rules that oil cannot be brought as a נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan depends on the לוג being a valid נדבה if the person is not a מצורע. רבי שמעון holds that oil is not a valid נדבה. So the plan seems to contradict his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: one may not donate oil as a gift offering

phrases.english: But didn't רבי שמעון say:
one may not donate oil!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge, this time to the basis of the whole plan
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan of a conditional נדבה of oil, according to רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון does not allow a נדבה of oil, so the 'if not, it is a נדבה' half of the condition seems to fail.

steps.title: Fixing a person's status is different
steps.stepSummary: The answer: when the oil is needed so a person can become purified, רבי שמעון allows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The remedy of a person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון's rule against donating oil does not apply when it is the only way to fix this person's status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's general rule stays in place. This case is an exception: the person has no other way to become purified. So רבי שמעון allows the oil here.

keyTerms.meaning: fixing (purifying) a person
is different

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון forbids donating oil in general, but makes an exception when it is needed to purify a person.

phrases.english: The remedy of a person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי שמעון's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון never allows a נדבה of oil
steps.terutzMaskana: When it is needed to purify a person, רבי שמעון allows the oil.

steps.title: Why not make it a provisional guilt offering?
steps.stepSummary: רב רחומי, quoting רב הונא בר תחליפא, asks why the doubtful מצורע does not say that if he is not a מצורע, his animal will be an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב רחומי sat before רבינא and said in the name of רב הונא בר תחליפא: Let him say, 'This אשם will be an אשם תלוי!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב רחומי suggests a better back-up plan for the doubtful מצורע's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי שמעון's plan, the back-up is a שלמים, which then has to be eaten in less time than usual. רב רחומי says an אשם תלוי is eaten for one day and night, just like the מצורע's אשם, so no time would be cut short. He is asking why רבי שמעון did not use this easier option.

keyTerms.meaning: A provisional guilt offering, brought by someone unsure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת
But let him say
Before him, in front of him

phrases.english: Rav Rechumi was sitting before Ravina,
and he was sitting and saying
in the name of Rav Huna bar Tachlifa:

phrases.aramaic: וְנֵימָא, אָשָׁם זֶה יְהֵא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי!
phrases.english: But let him say: this guilt offering shall be a provisional guilt offering!
phrases.notes: He means the back-up: if I am not a מצורע, this animal is an אשם תלוי instead of a שלמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא, אָשָׁם זֶה יְהֵא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי שמעון's stipulation plan for the doubtful מצורע and suggests a better back-up option.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's choice of a שלמים as the back-up identity of the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אשם תלוי has the same eating time as the מצורע's אשם, so it would avoid cutting short the time for a שלמים.

steps.title: Proof that רבי שמעון forbids donating an אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון did not suggest the אשם תלוי option, רב רחומי concludes that רבי שמעון is the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר and holds that one may not donate an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: who is the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר? It is רבי שמעון, who says one may not donate an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב רחומי uses the question he just asked to draw a conclusion about רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a person may bring an אשם תלוי as a voluntary donation. רב רחומי reasons that רבי שמעון skipped the אשם תלוי option because he holds it cannot be donated. That would make רבי שמעון the unnamed תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude
A sage from the time of the משנה
One may not bring it as a voluntary donation

phrases.english: Learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר –
phrases.english: who is the tanna who disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר holds you may bring an אשם תלוי as a voluntary donation.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon,
who says: one may not donate a provisional guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question from step 8 into a proof about רבי שמעון's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds one may not donate an אשם תלוי, against רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's silence about the אשם תלוי option in the doubtful מצורע case

steps.title: רבינא: lambs are not rams
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the proof. The מצורע's אשם is a lamb, but an אשם תלוי must be a ram, so the animal could never be an אשם תלוי anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Torah, Torah! You are mixing up lambs with rams!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא knocks down both רב רחומי's suggestion and his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע brings a one-year-old lamb as his אשם, while an אשם תלוי must be a ram in its second year. One animal cannot fit both, so רבי שמעון had no choice and could not have suggested an אשם תלוי. His silence proves nothing about whether one may donate an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A cry of surprise: where is your Torah knowledge?
Lambs, which are in their first year
Rams, which are in their second year
Are being mixed up

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם מצורע is a lamb and an אשם תלוי is a ram, so one animal cannot be set aside for both. The proof about רבי שמעון falls away.

phrases.english: He said to him: Torah, Torah!
phrases.notes: רבינא is saying in surprise: a learned man like you should know this!

phrases.english: You are confusing lambs with rams!
phrases.notes: The מצורע's אשם is a lamb (ויקרא 14:10). An אשם תלוי is a ram (ויקרא 5:15).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תּוֹרָה תּוֹרָה! אִימְּרֵי בְּדִיכְרֵי מִיחַלְּפִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects both the suggestion in step 8 and the proof in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both the suggestion that the back-up could be an אשם תלוי and the proof drawn from it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The animals are different: the מצורע's אשם is a lamb, while an אשם תלוי must be a ram.

steps.title: משנה: limbs of a sin offering mixed with limbs of a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: Limbs of a חטאת got mixed with limbs of an עולה. רבי אליעזר says to put them all on the מזבח and treat the חטאת meat as wood. The חכמים say to wait until they become unfit and then burn them all in the בית השריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Limbs of a חטאת mixed with limbs of an עולה: רבי אליעזר says to put them all up on the מזבח, and he views the חטאת meat up there as if it were wood. The חכמים say to let their form spoil, and then they all go out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case of mixed offerings and a disagreement about what to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of a חטאת is eaten by כהנים and may not go on the מזבח, but an עולה is burned completely on the מזבח. Since no one can tell the pieces apart, רבי אליעזר lets everything go up and treats the חטאת meat as plain wood fuel. The חכמים do not allow this. They wait until all the pieces become unfit and then burn them where unfit offerings are burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs of a sin offering
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Wood, the fuel burned on the מזבח
Let their form spoil, meaning wait until they become unfit by sitting overnight
The place where unfit offerings are burned

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say the חטאת meat becomes a קרבן on the מזבח. He says it goes up only as wood, not as an offering.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵיבְרֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בְּאֵיבְרֵי עוֹלָה –
phrases.english: MISHNA: Limbs of a sin offering that became mixed with limbs of a burnt offering:
Rabbi Eliezer says: he should place them above,

phrases.aramaic: וְרוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת בְּשַׂר הַחַטָּאת מִלְּמַעְלָה
phrases.english: and I view the flesh of the sin offering up there
as if it were wood.
And the Rabbis say: let their form decay,
phrases.notes: He means: leave them until they become unfit, and only then burn them.

phrases.english: and they should go out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵיבְרֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בְּאֵיבְרֵי עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new case, separate from the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: put all the mixed limbs on the מזבח and treat the חטאת meat as wood. חכמים: wait until all become unfit, then burn them in the בית השריפה.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's source for putting forbidden meat on the מזבח as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for רבי אליעזר's source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the meat of a חטאת on the מזבח seems to break the rule that it may not be offered there. So the גמרא needs to know what lets רבי אליעזר treat it as wood.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that allows putting non-offerable meat on the מזבח as wood

steps.title: The verse: not as a pleasing aroma, but as wood
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says forbidden items 'shall not go up as a pleasing aroma.' רבי אליעזר learns that they cannot go up as an offering, but they may go up as wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'But they shall not go up on the מזבח as a pleasing aroma.' You may not offer them up as a pleasing aroma, but you may offer them up as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that רבי אליעזר reads closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not simply say forbidden things may not go on the מזבח. It says they may not go up 'as a pleasing aroma,' which means as an offering. רבי אליעזר learns from this that they may go up as fuel, which is why the חטאת meat can be burned as wood.

keyTerms.meaning: As a pleasing aroma, meaning as a real offering
For the sake of wood, meaning as fuel only

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר reads 'לא יעלו לריח ניחח' as banning forbidden things only as offerings, not as wood. That is how the חטאת meat can go up on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לֹא יַעֲלוּ לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ –
phrases.english: The verse states: "But they shall not come up for a pleasing aroma on the altar"
as a pleasing aroma you may not offer them up,
but you may offer them up for the sake of wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְאֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לֹא יַעֲלוּ לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 2:12 bans forbidden items on the מזבח only 'as a pleasing aroma,' so they may go up as wood.

steps.title: The רבנן limit the wood rule to leaven and honey
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read ״אֹתָם״ as a limit. Only leaven and honey may go up on the מזבח as wood. Other forbidden things may not go up at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? The Torah limits it with the word 'them.' It is only them that you may not bring up as an offering, but you may bring them up as wood. But anything else may not go up at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן deal with רבי אליעזר's reading of the פסוק. They say the wood rule applies only to leaven and honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned that forbidden items may go up on the מזבח 'as wood.' The רבנן agree this is true, but they say the word ״אֹתָם״ limits it to the items the פסוק is talking about: leaven and honey. So חטאת meat, or any other forbidden item, cannot be put on the מזבח even as wood.

keyTerms.meaning: excluded or limited; the word narrows the rule
the Merciful One; a way of saying 'the Torah'
'them'; the word in the פסוק that limits the rule
as wood; as fuel, not as an offering
something else; other items

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? The Torah limited it with the word 'them'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:12. 'Them' means the leaven and honey mentioned in the פסוק before it.

phrases.english: It is them that you may not bring up as an offering,
but you may bring them up as wood.
But anything else may not go up at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's answer to רבי אליעזר's source from Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do the רבנן answer רבי אליעזר's reading of 'they shall not go up as a pleasing aroma'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אֹתָם״ limits the wood rule to leaven and honey only. Other forbidden items may not go up at all.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר uses the word 'them' for the ramp
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses ״אֹתָם״ for a different lesson. Only for leaven and honey is the ramp treated like the מזבח itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? He says it is only them for which the Torah included the ramp as being like the altar. But for other things, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר does with the limiting word ״אֹתָם״. It answers that he learns a different lesson from it, about the ramp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אליעזר lets forbidden items go up as wood, he cannot use ״אֹתָם״ the way the רבנן do. Instead, he says the word teaches that only for leaven and honey is bringing them onto the כֶּבֶשׁ treated like bringing them onto the מזבח. For other forbidden items, the ramp is not treated that way.

keyTerms.meaning: included; the פסוק adds something to the rule
the ramp that leads up to the מזבח
like the מזבח itself

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, what does he learn from 'them'?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתָם הוּא דְּרַבַּאי לָךְ כֶּבֶשׁ כְּמִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: It is only them for which the Torah included the ramp as being like the altar,
but for other things, it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – אוֹתָם הוּא דְּרַבַּאי לָךְ כֶּבֶשׁ כְּמִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי אליעזר uses the same word the רבנן used in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי אליעזר learn from the limiting word ״אֹתָם״?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only for leaven and honey is the ramp treated like the מזבח.

steps.title: The רבנן learn both lessons from 'them'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn two lessons from ״אֹתָם״: the wood rule and the ramp rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the רבנן get the ramp rule, since they already used ״אֹתָם״ for the wood rule. It answers that they learn both rules from the one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the רבנן had already used ״אֹתָם״ up. The answer is that, for them, the word limits everything in the פסוק to leaven and honey. That covers both going up as wood and the ramp being treated like the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: two things
learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that ״אֹתָם״ is a limiting word. רבי אליעזר uses it only for the ramp rule. The רבנן use it for both the ramp rule and the wood rule, so for them only leaven and honey may go up as wood.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, where do they learn the ramp rule?
They learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the רבנן can also get the ramp rule from Step 15 out of the same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do the רבנן get the ramp rule?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They learn both the wood rule and the ramp rule from ״אֹתָם״.

steps.title: רבי יהודה tells the argument differently from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה does not match רבי יהודה. He says רבי אליעזר and the חכמים agree that mixed חטאת and עולה limbs are offered, and agree that limbs mixed with a רובע or נרבע are not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא. As it was taught: רבי יהודה said, רבי אליעזר and the חכמים did not argue about limbs of a sin offering that got mixed with limbs of a burnt offering: they are offered. With an animal that mated with a person, or that a person mated with, they are not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה tells the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים differently from our משנה. This opens a new topic: if they agree on these cases, where do they argue?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about חטאת limbs mixed with עולה limbs. רבי יהודה says they agree here: the limbs are offered. They also agree that limbs mixed with a רובע or נרבע are not offered. So, according to him, their argument must be about some other case.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
a teacher from the time of the משנה
they did not argue
an animal that mated with a person, or that a person mated with; it may not be brought on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה is just repeating our משנה. He is saying that the case our משנה presents as an argument is actually agreed on by both sides.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah does not follow this Tanna,
as it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages did not argue

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֵיבְרֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בְּאֵיבְרֵי עוֹלָה – שֶׁיִּקְרְבוּ;
phrases.english: about limbs of a sin offering that got mixed with limbs of a burnt offering: they are offered;
with an animal that mated with a person, or that a person mated with: they are not offered.
phrases.notes: He means good limbs that got mixed with limbs of such an animal. Both sides agree none of them go on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the פסוק and returns to the משנה's case from Step 11, showing that another תנא tells the argument differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, everyone agrees that mixed חטאת and עולה limbs are offered, and everyone agrees that limbs mixed with a רובע or נרבע are not offered.

steps.title: Where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים really argue: blemished limbs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the real argument is about kosher עולה limbs mixed with limbs of a blemished animal. רבי אליעזר lets them all be offered and treats the blemished limbs as wood. The חכמים forbid offering any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they argue about? About limbs of a kosher עולה that got mixed with limbs of a blemished animal. רבי אליעזר says: offer them all, and I look at the blemished limbs on top of the מזבח as if they were wood. The חכמים say: do not offer them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה is still talking. He told us where the two sides agree, and now he names the one case where they argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is limited to a בעלת מום mixed with a kosher עולה. רבי אליעזר's reason, 'I see them as wood,' matches what we saw in step 13: a forbidden item may go up as wood, just not as an offering. The חכמים say the blemished limbs cannot go up at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering with no blemish, fully kosher for the מזבח
An animal with a blemish, which may not be brought on the מזבח
Got mixed together, so you cannot tell which is which
They shall be offered
Wood, the fuel burned on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the only argument is about blemished limbs. רבי אליעזר treats them as wood and offers everything. The חכמים offer nothing.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About the limbs of an unblemished burnt offering
that got mixed with the limbs of a blemished animal,
for רבי אליעזר says: they shall be offered,
and I view them up above
phrases.notes: He means the blemished limbs once they are on top of the מזבח.

phrases.english: as if they are wood;
and the חכמים say: they shall not be offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יהודה's statement from step 17 by naming the one case where the two sides argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kosher עולה limbs mixed with blemished limbs: רבי אליעזר says offer all, with the blemished limbs counting as wood. The חכמים say do not offer them.

steps.title: Why is a רובע or נרבע worse than a blemished animal for רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר treats a בעלת מום as wood but does not do the same for a רובע or נרבע. None of them is fit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אליעזר, what makes a רובע or נרבע different? If you say it is because they are not fit, a blemished animal is not fit either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view as רבי יהודה reported it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, רבי יהודה said both sides agree that limbs mixed with a רובע or נרבע are not offered. But in step 18, רבי אליעזר lets blemished limbs go up as wood. Since 'not fit' describes all three, the גמרא wants to know why the wood idea does not also cover the רובע and נרבע.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? Asks why two cases that look alike get different rulings
An animal that had relations with a person
An animal that a person had relations with
Fit (for the מזבח)
Also, too

phrases.english: And according to רבי אליעזר,
what is different about a רובע and a נרבע
that you would say they are not fit?
A blemished animal is also not fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַאי שְׁנָא רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two rulings from steps 17 and 18 to point out what looks like a contradiction in רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling as reported by רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'not fit' does not stop blemished limbs from going up as wood, it should not stop רובע and נרבע limbs either. So why does רבי אליעזר agree they are not offered?
